angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,855,153 km at 106.90 pc = 0.36 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 74961: distance 106.896 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.026), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 106.896 +/- 2.779 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 9.5255 +/- 0.0164 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09), 580.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 4.104 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 74961: radius 4.104 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 8.448 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.057) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 2,855,153 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4861 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 74961: effective temperature 4861 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.022) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 74961: effective temperature 4861 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.022) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.38 from 2024A&A...691A..53S; the 11 published values span log g 3.38 to 3.6, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...691A..53S)
